title: Insecure PATH Inheritance and Environment Trust
platform_conditions: POSIX sh and bash on Linux/macOS; bash skips BASH_ENV and sourced functions under setuid invocation, but root shell contexts without -p still honor inherited PATH, IFS and exported functions
security_mechanism: An unqualified command name is resolved by walking $PATH left to right at call time, so in a privileged context an attacker-controlled PATH entry placed first supplies a substitute executable that runs with the script's privileges. The same trust surface includes IFS (inherited through some older shells' environments, changing every unquoted expansion), BASH_ENV/ENV (pointing bash/sh at an attacker-writable startup file that executes before the script body), LD_PRELOAD and _dyld_* variables, and exported function definitions, which a child bash imports and can therefore replace a utility's behavior wholesale.

source_sink_clues.source: Environment inherited from an untrusted caller: setuid or sudo-invoked scripts, CI runners triggered by untrusted pull requests, cron/systemd jobs whose environment an attacker can influence, and any wrapper invoked with env or a user-modified PATH.
source_sink_clues.sink: Unqualified command names (tar, grep, awk, helper scripts) executed in a privileged script without a pinned PATH; scripts that read BASH_ENV/ENV-honored startup files; shells started with inherited exported functions; use of IFS from the environment

tracking_guards: Check the script pins PATH to a fixed list of root-owned directories at the top (PATH=/usr/bin:/bin; export PATH) and invokes security-critical binaries by absolute path; check setuid scripts use setpriv/env -i or bash -p so inherited env is dropped; check IFS is reset explicitly (IFS=$' \t\n'); check exported functions are unset (-f) before privilege-sensitive work.
not_candidate_when: PATH is pinned to a constant, root-owned list before the first command and security-relevant binaries are called by absolute path, the script only ever runs from a trusted operator environment (interactive root shell, locked-down CI image) where no untrusted party can set variables, or the script runs under env -i / bash -p so the inherited environment is empty by construction.
public_references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
Bash Reference Manual: Bash Variables (PATH, BASH_ENV, PS4) — https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Bash-Variables.html
